content: The test image shows soybean pods and stems that are dark brown, shriveled, and dried-looking. No leaves visible. The pods appear blighted/discolored uniformly brown-reddish. This pattern on pods + stems points toward pod blight diseases — Phomopsis or Diaporthe are top candidates.

The Phomopsis reference shows brown/blighted pods with circular lesion patterns in some images, and simple brown dried pods in others (top-right quadrant). The test image shows uniformly dark brown, shriveled soybean pods on dried stems — matching the pod blight presentation of Phomopsis.

Key visual match:
- Brown shriveled pods hanging from thin dried stems — matches Phomopsis top-right reference
- Uniform dark browning of pods without green tissue remaining
- No white mycelium (rules out White_Mold), no leaf symptoms (not a foliar disease)
